newsitem.title: USA: Showers seen for western U.S. Midwest, east dry.
newsitem.headline: Showers seen for western U.S. Midwest, east dry.

text.p: Scattered to widely scattered showers were forecast for parts of western Iowa and eastern Nebraska over the weekend while the rest of the corn belt was expected to be warm and dry, Weather Services Corp said.

"Beginning on late Saturday and probably again on Sunday, there would be the risk of some scattered to widely scattered storms with rainfall amounts of .25 to .75 inch and locally heavier," said WSC meteorologist Joel Burgio.
The forecast was based on late morning National Weather Service weather map updates, Burgio said.
Coverage was expected to be 50 percent in western Iowa and eastern Nebraska, he said.
There was no precipitation in the forecast through Sunday for areas east of the Mississippi River, Burgio said.
Temperatures across the corn belt were expected to top out in the low to mid 80s Farenheit, he said.
